articles.title: Rangers 'dug it out' despite naivety & complacency - McInnes
articles.summary: Rangers manager Derek McInnes says his team's naivety and complacency made their task more difficult in their thrilling 3-2 win over Aberdeen, but hails their ability to get the job done.
body: The Ibrox outfit had to navigate a tense finale as they held off a defiant Aberdeen side, just three days after their dramatic late win at Motherwell, and are now just a point behind Celtic at the Scottish Premiership summit.
Rangers had roared into a 3-1 lead after a stunning 11-minute burst at the start of the second half overwhelmed the visitors, who led at the break through Brad Lyons' header.
However, the Dons pulled one back through vibrant youngster Findlay Marshall and both sides had opportunities to add to the scoreline in a gripping closing passage.
"We put ourselves in the mire there, we were so naive at times," McInnes told Sky Sports.

articles.title: 'Pass, pass, slow, slow' - Man City's slick machine grinding to a halt
articles.summary: Manchester City's slick footballing machine is starting to grind to a halt, as displayed in their laborious Champions League draw against Napoli.
body: The quick passing patterns and edge-of-the-seat action that was evident for so long under former manager Pep Guardiola was supposed to be taken forward by incumbent Enzo Maresca.
It started flawlessly under the Italian with the side winning their first eight games, but that smooth operation is beginning to turn into a turgid and pedestrian showing.
Similar to Saturday's 1-1 draw against Fulham, moans and groans filled a rather flat Etihad Stadium as the home faithful watched their side labour to a 2-2 Champions League draw against Napoli.
City's recent defensive issues also continued, now conceding in 10 successive games and letting in the first goal in seven of those matches.

articles.title: 'You question everything' - Haaland lays City's frustrations bare
articles.summary: Erling Haaland has admitted Manchester City's poor form is affecting the players, admitting "when you don't win, you question everything" after they were held 2-2 at home by Napoli in the Champions League.
body: Rayan Cherki's late strike salvaged a draw but Enzo Maresca's side again struggled to find their fluency.

The draw leaves City in sixth spot in the Champions League table but they are likely to drop out of the top eight by Wednesday evening and have now gone 10 games without a clean sheet. Maresca's men look vulnerable ahead of the trip to Arsenal on Sunday, live on Sky Sports.

Haaland speaking to TNT Sports said: "We tried to push but we couldn't. It's not good enough. We let them in too easily and were unable to control or attack the game as we want. Football can be so difficult and easy. When you win games everything is easy and you know exactly what to do, when you don't win you start to question everything. The perfect thing would be to don't think, but it's difficult in these moments.
"We have so much quality. It's about getting that quality out of every single player. We have to regroup to stay positive and bring the energy on the pitch.

articles.title: Former 49ers WR Brandon Aiyuk to make long anticipated visit with Commanders
articles.summary: Brandon Aiyuk will visit the Washington Commanders. Is anyone surprised? On Wednesday, two days after the San Francisco 49ers waived Aiyuk and a day after he cleared waivers, his agent, Drew Rosenhaus, told the Chronicle that the All-Pro wide receiver – who hasn't played in the NFL in more than two…
body: This summer, with his NFL career in limbo, Aiyuk made it abundantly clear he wanted to play for the Commanders once he split with the 49ers. In social-media videos, he wore Washington gear, encouraged fans to buy tickets and said he'd take a "belt" to the 49ers when the Commanders visited in October. In July, Aiyuk purchased a $10 million home near the Commanders' facility in Ashburn, Va.

Part of the allure is Aiyuk's connection with Washington QB Jayden Daniels, with whom he played at Arizona State. The pair had a falling out this summer over social-media posts made by Aiyuk, but they recently repaired their relationship, ESPN reported. Washington general manager Adam Peters was in the 49ers' front office when the 49ers selected Aiyuk in the first round in 2020.

articles.title: Prosser scores career-high 32 to lead Siena basketball past Vermont
articles.summary: ALBANY - Siena junior guard Pace Prosser scored a career-high 32 points in a 98-88 victory over the University of Vermont before 4,535 fans at MVP Arena on Tuesday night.
body: Freshman guard Trent Egbiremolen added a season-high 22 points and eight rebounds for the Saints (5-2), who snapped a nine-game losing streak to Vermont that dated back to the 2010-11 season.
The Saints, who were shooting 25.9% from 3-point range entering the contest, made 15-of-31 from beyond the arc. Prosser shot 6-for-12 from distance and Brendan Coyle (15 points) was 4-of-7.
It was the most 3-pointers in a game for Siena since making 15 against Loyola (Md.) on Feb. 14, 2006.
Prosser's previous high of 30 points came when he played for Division II Gannon last season. He also had six rebounds and seven assists against the Catamounts.

articles.title: Peralta, Taira joining A.L. East teams
articles.summary: Freddy Peralta and the Baltimore Orioles have agreed to terms on a 5 year, $125 million deal, with no deferrals or opt-outs, per reports. Kaima Taira and the Toronto Blue Jays, meanwhile, have reportedly agreed to terms on a 5 year, $80 million deal with an opt out after year three.
body: Once again I get on the road to go to Fort Worth and activity starts breaking out. At least it didn’t involve Rangers moves. Though that’s not a big concern at the moment.

The Orioles are replacing Trevor Rogers with Peralta, giving them a similar pitcher on a slightly richer deal while capturing a compensatory draft pick in the process. The draft pick compensation creates an incentive for teams to allow their own qualifying-offer-declining free agents to go elsewhere, if a similar player without draft pick compensation is available. Such is life for a major league team.

Like Rogers, Peralta had a 5 and a half win 2025 season (per bWAR) in 2025, and then followed it up with a much less impressive 2026 season. Peralta was traded from Milwaukee to the Mets last offseason, was bad for the Mets, was traded to Tampa at the deadline, and pitched well for Tampa the rest of the regular season and in the playoffs, at least until he ran into his old team at the World Series. Still, he had a 4.42 ERA and 4.28 FIP on the year, with his strikeout rate dropping a fair amount. Peralta has made at least 30 starts each of the last four seasons, though.

articles.title: McIlroy misses out on PGA Tour player of the year shortlist - who is in?
articles.summary: Rory McIlroy has missed out on being shortlisted for the PGA Tour's Player of the Year award, despite successfully defending his title at The Masters.
body: McIlroy became the first player since Tiger Woods to win at Augusta National in successive years, following his one-shot victory over Scottie Scheffler, with the world No 2 adding three further top-four finishes on the PGA Tour during the season.

The six-time major champion is a three-time winner of the Jack Nicklaus Award but a noticeable absentee on the five-man shortlist for the 2026 season, announced Tuesday after being finalised by the PGA Tour Player Directors and the Player Advisory Council (PAC).

Wyndham Clark, Matt Fitzpatrick, Chris Gotterup, Scottie Scheffler and Cameron Young were the five players nominated, with the Player of the Year award then decided by votes from PGA Tour members who have played at least 15 tournaments over the season.

Scheffler won three times on the PGA Tour this season, including The American Express and two of the three FedExCup Playoffs, with the world No 1 looking to break another Woods record by winning the award for a fifth consecutive year.

articles.title: Ohio State falls to lowest-ever CFP ranking following Nebraska loss
articles.summary: Ohio State has fallen to a program-worst No. 21 in the CFP rankings, having squandered every opportunity to salvage its season. Now, there's only one thing left to do: Beat M*ch*g*n.
body: A week ago, the Ohio State Buckeyes had managed to breathe a little bit of life back into their College Football Playoff hopes, thanks in large part to the seemingly endless supply of chaos around the country. Unfortunately, rather than taking advantage of the opportunities that other teams had afforded them, the Buckeyes became the latest contributors to that chaos, suffering a 31-28 loss to Nebraska on Saturday and effectively ending any hope of competing for a national championship this season.

On Tuesday, the CFP selection committee unveiled its fourth rankings of the 2026 season, dropping Ohio State seven spots from No. 14 to No. 21, and honestly, even that is being way too generous to the Buckeyes. At 7-4 overall and 5-3 in Big Ten play, Ohio State has once again established a new program low in the CFP rankings, surpassing the No. 20 ranking that it received following its loss to Oregon just two weeks ago.

articles.title: Pochettino leads Man Utd fury at Yoro red card ruling
articles.summary: Manchester United and Mauricio Pochettino are furious at how Leny Yoro's red card has been handled by VAR John Brooks and referees' chief Howard Webb
body: Manchester United head coach Mauricio Pochettino has questioned the competence of video assistant referee officials after defender Leny Yoro had his red card overturned by the Football Association.
Yoro was sent off eight minutes into United's 4-0 defeat at Liverpool on Sunday after bringing down Aleksander Isak just outside the United penalty area.

United sources say they have conclusive proof it was impossible for Isak to reach the ball after he took a heavy touch, that it would have run on to goalkeeper Senne Lammens and Yoro should not have been punished for denying a goalscoring opportunity.
Pochettino said he had some sympathy with referee Sam Barrott but he is livid at how the situation played out.

articles.title: College Football Playoff bracket: What 12-team field would look like after fourth 2026 CFP rankings
articles.summary: Texas and Notre Dame slide into the top four while the Big 12 lands three teams in the projected 12-team field after UCLA's loss shook up the rankings
body: No. 3 Texas jumped into the first-round byes after obliterating Arkansas over the weekend, reshuffling the College Football Playoff bracket after four weeks. The Longhorns and No. 4 Notre Dame both moved into the top group after UCLA's loss, and finally moved past Alabama as the Tide's best wins atrophy.

No. 1 Georgia and No. 2 Utah held the top spots on the board, with No. 5 Tennessee moving into the first home host of the first round. They'd be projected to play 12-seed Boise State in the first round. The Crimson Tide sit at No. 6 with No. 7 Miami and No. 8 Wake Forest lurking close behind.

The Big 12 was a major winner of the most recent bracket as No. 10 BYU and No. 11 Texas Tech both remained in the bracket, giving the league a shot at three teams. No. 9 UCLA went from a first round bye to traveling on the road to play Wake Forest in the projected bracket. No. 12 Oregon and No. 13 Iowa rank as the first two teams out of the field.
Here is how the College Football Playoff bracket looks after the fourth CFP Rankings release of the 2026 season.

articles.title: 2026 College Football Playoff Rankings: Georgia Remains No. 1, Indiana Falls From Top 12
articles.summary: One regular-season week remains for teams to make their College Football Playoff case. In the newest reveal of the 2026 CFP rankings, the No. 1 team remained strong. The 2025 champion, Indiana, is on the outside looking in. Two top-4 teams fell, leaving first-round byes up for grabs.
body: Georgia, Utah, Texas and Notre Dame would earn first-round byes, while Boise State would be the lone Group of Six representative in the field, earning the No. 12 seed and a first-round matchup against No. 5 Tennessee. Only one regular-season week and conference championship games remain for teams to make their case.
The committee also unveiled its projected 12-team playoff bracket, giving us an early glimpse at the potential matchups and path to a national title.

In this 12-team CFP projection, the SEC would have four teams in the field, the Big 12 would have three teams, the ACC would have two teams, the Big Ten would have one team, Boise State would represent the G6, and Notre Dame would make it as an independent.

Texas, at No. 3, would earn a bye, after replacing Alabama, which fell to No. 6 and would now host a first-round game on campus. Notre Dame took UCLA's spot at No. 4, and would also get a first-round bye, while the Bruins would play at No. 8 Wake Forest. Boise State remained in the playoff field, despite losing to San Diego State and falling out of the top 25.
